questions.q: What does an outcome reward model (ORM) evaluate when scoring a reasoning trace?
options: Every intermediate step's logical validity
Only whether the final answer matches ground truth, ignoring the reasoning in between
The number of tokens in the trace
The fluency of the writing style
questions.explain: An ORM checks only the destination — if the final answer matches, the trace gets full reward regardless of how it got there.

questions.q: Why can a process reward model (PRM) help with credit assignment compared to a pure terminal (outcome-only) reward?
options: It eliminates the need for a value function entirely
It gives a score to each intermediate step directly, rather than requiring the advantage estimator to propagate one terminal number backward through an entire long trace
It makes the trace shorter
It removes the need for a policy network
questions.explain: Per-step rewards supply intermediate signal directly, reducing the high-variance burden on the value function/advantage estimator to reconstruct credit from a single endpoint.

questions.q: What did OpenAI's "Let's Verify Step by Step" find when comparing a PRM and an ORM trained on the same math problems?
options: The ORM was strictly better in every respect
The PRM was a meaningfully better reward signal, ranking candidate solutions better and generalizing further because it rewards sound reasoning rather than just a matching final answer
Both performed identically
Neither could be trained successfully
questions.explain: The paper found the process-supervised reward model out-performed the outcome-supervised one on math reasoning tasks.

questions.q: What is the Math-Shepherd approach to labeling process reward steps, and why does it matter?
options: It requires every step to be labeled by a human expert
It labels a step by sampling many continuations from it and checking what fraction reach the correct final answer, automating step-level supervision without human review of each step
It only works for code, not math
It replaces the need for any reward signal at all
questions.explain: Math-Shepherd estimates a step's quality via sampled rollouts' success rate, similar in spirit to Monte Carlo value estimation, reducing reliance on costly human step labels like those in PRM800K.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how do outcome reward and process reward typically get used together in practice?
options: They are never combined in the same system
Outcome reward tends to dominate large-scale RL training because it is cheap at high rollout volume, while process reward earns its cost in roles where it is reused many times, such as guiding search
Process reward is always used for RL training and outcome reward is never used
Outcome reward can only be used on code, never on math
questions.explain: The lesson describes outcome reward as cheap and dominant for large-scale training, while process reward's higher cost is best justified in reused roles like guiding test-time search.
